subject: accessing transformed variables does not work group-wise

messages.author: 91481440fd4fef18
messages.subject: accessing transformed variables does not work group-wise
parts:
I thought I'd mention it here since I found it to be counter-
intuitive. If I have a data frame with a factor variable I can easily
perform statistics with ggplot2 per group but when I tried the
following I was thrown off:

my.var <- rnorm(1000)
my.type <- rep(1:4, each=250)
tmp$type <- factor(tmp$type)
tmp <- data.frame(var=my.var, type=my.type)

ggplot(tmp, aes(x=var, y=..count../sum(..count..), colour=type,
group=type)) + geom_freqpoly(binwidth=0.5)

dividing the observed ..count.. by sum(..count..) does not work group-
wise but instead divides by the sum over the whole ..count.. column.

ggb <- ggplot_build(last_plot())
> sum(ggb$data[[1]][[1]]$y)
[1] 1

I know how to avoid this problem for now but it was very unexpected.

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: accessing transformed variables does not work group-wise
parts:
Hi Moritz,

Yes, because that happens at a a completely different stage of the
processing cycle. I'm not sure if this is something worth fixing
(because it would have substantial performance implications), but it's
just of the things that make it a good idea to do the majority of your
data manipulation outside of ggplot2.

Hadley
